title: Gibbs-Policy Regret under Annealed Penalties with a Mixed Atom and Dose Window
banked_reason: The restricted calibration regime and absent operational evidence constrain the projected paper score despite the delivered matching bounds; paper_score_ceiling 6 < field floor 7.4.
gap_reasons: The delivered result is a matched local minimax phase diagram for penalty-dependent alternatives with a public quadratic baseline, known mode, localized uncertainty, and a deliberately synchronized logarithmic comparator offset. It does not establish a penalty-path frontier for a fixed response law or account for uncertainty in those calibration quantities, which limits its econometric reach. The certificate establishes computable termination but delivers no full-class numerical bracket or finite-sample policy evaluation; its enormous comparison constants and unrestricted computational cost leave the prospective planning application unsupported. The closest comparator's [public theorem text](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.19230v3) concerns fixed-positive-penalty finite-dimensional assignment rules, so it does not subsume this mixed-law decision experiment. The framing preserves the triangular-class restriction and the distinction between experiment equivalence and decision-risk convergence, with no stale claim promoting an open step into a theorem. proof_attempt_summary: Two discovery solve rounds delivered the critical mixed comparator-dose game and a five-regime penalty-path strengthening, including matching bounds, effective transfer, finite-program certificates and allocation laws. The informal math and decision reviews passed and all six foundational citations were verified. Independent main validity review confirmed that public calibration, triangular local alternatives and missing operational evidence cap this package at incremental tier; no formalization was launched.
tldr: On a declared compact-support \(C^2\) triangular dose-response class, the penalty path \(\lambda_{n,\alpha}=n^{-\alpha}\) has two information elbows. The dose scale is \(n\lambda_{n,\alpha}^{5/2}\) and the comparator scale is \(n\lambda_{n,\alpha}^{2}\). Normalized causal Gibbs-policy regret tends to zero below \(2/5\), to the finite-dose Gaussian game at \(2/5\), to an observed-offset dose-blind game between \(2/5\) and \(1/2\), to a finite-comparator Gaussian game at \(1/2\), and to a no-information game above \(1/2\). The nonzero constants have explicit convergent convex-program certificates and matching original-data policies. Exact-parameter rows are decision-risk limits; the critical comparison retains its finite comparator noise. The selected mixed-policy allocation laws are characterized on this same class.
gap: Fixed-positive-penalty mixed-treatment analysis does not characterize the decision value at a shrinking interior mode. Scalar nonlinear-regret treatment choice does not optimize the entire dose density jointly with a comparator probability.
fill: Uniform finite-noise experiment comparison, legal inner meshes, a bounded Bayes-action reduction, and two-sided convex-program certificates characterize the causal regret constant and an attaining policy. A finite-bin comparison handle specifies a candidate error envelope, a polynomial mesh schedule, and pilot and decision tolerances. Their certification and the minimax constant must be derived.
